title: Gopali v. State of U.P. through Secretary and others
coram: S.P. Mehrotra, J. & Het Singh Yadav, J.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed on the ground of availability of the alternative remedy of a statutory appeal
headnote: A writ against a final assessment order under Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 will not be entertained where the controversy is basically factual and an appeal under Section 127 read with Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is available. On a checking (24.3.2011) a provisional assessment (4.7.2011) and demand notice were issued; after an earlier writ directed disposal of the consumer's objection, the Executive Engineer dismissed it (26.9.2012). The Court accepted the licensee's preliminary objection and, noting that s.126 provides for provisional assessment, objections and a final order after hearing, and s.127 r/w Clause 6.8 provides the appeal, dismissed the writ on the ground of alternative remedy, the factual controversy being fit for the appellate forum. (Closely parallels SCJ-224, Moolchand Saini, another Mehrotra-Bench dismissal on the same footing.)

holding_units.clause: s.127 (r/w Clause 6.8, U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005)
holding_units.topic: Writ against a final s.126 assessment declined where the s.127 appeal is available and the dispute is factual
holding_units.question: Should a writ against a final Section 126 assessment be entertained where the controversy is factual and an appeal under Section 127 r/w Clause 6.8 is available?
holding_units.holding: No. Section 126 provides for provisional assessment, objections and a final order after hearing; Section 127(1) gives a right of appeal against the final order, and Clause 6.8 likewise provides for an appeal. As the controversy was basically factual and better decided in appeal, the Court accepted the preliminary objection and dismissed the writ on the ground of the available alternative remedy.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Checking 24.3.2011; provisional assessment 4.7.2011; objection dismissed by EE on 26.9.2012 after an earlier writ directed its disposal; challenge basically factual.

principle_tags.application: A factual challenge to a final s.126 assessment is not entertained in writ jurisdiction where the s.127 appeal (r/w Clause 6.8) is available.
The statutory appeal is the appropriate forum for a fact-heavy assessment dispute; existence of the remedy warrants declining the writ.

not_decided.point: The merits of the checking and the final assessment
not_decided.note: Left to the s.127 appellate authority; the controversy was found to be basically factual.
